changes.text: At `min` / `max` a stepper stays focusable with `aria-disabled="true"` and becomes a no-op, so keyboard focus no longer drops to `<body>`. Native `disabled` is kept only when the field is `disabled` or `readonly`.

Stepper presses are announced: a visually hidden `<span class="live" aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true">` is always rendered and receives the new value, and both steppers carry `aria-controls` pointing at the input.
The stepper focus ring is a solid inset `2px` `--ss-primary` outline (was a faint `--ss-primary-soft` glow).
The required marker uses `margin-inline-start`, so it sits on the correct side under `dir="rtl"`.

Plain-HTML behaviour in `dssoca/vanilla.js` matches: steppers get `aria-disabled` at the bounds (native `disabled` only when the input is disabled or read-only), and a nudge writes the new value into the field's `.live` region when the markup has one.
Plain-HTML support: `dssoca/vanilla.js` wires the `.ss-numberfield .step` buttons to step the input by its `step`, clamp to `min` / `max`, and fire `input` and `change` events.
The invalid focus ring is built with `color-mix()` from `--ss-danger` instead of `rgba(var(--ss-red-rgb), 0.22)`, so it follows an imported palette.

New component: a numeric input with `−` / `+` stepper buttons, `min` / `max` / `step` clamping, a bindable `value` (`null` when empty) and a monospace value, with `label`, `hint`, `error` and `size` on the shared field chrome.
